q8.answer: The older run stops without deploying at the first gate that finds a newer merge. Usually that is the check that staging still runs its SHA, which runs before production starts. The run is marked superseded, not failed, no alert is raised, and a one-line note goes to #deploys. Open question: the diagram has no supersession check at the approval gate, so the stop happens after approval, not at the gate. I have not confirmed that this is the intended behaviour.

q9.answer: A run approved outside the Monday to Thursday, 09:00 to 15:00 UTC window waits for the next opening. It is exempt from the 72-hour expiry while it waits, and the window is checked once, just before production starts. I did not decide what happens when another production deploy holds the prod-deploy lock: whether the run waits, fails or is superseded is not specified, though the lock is what keeps production to one deploy at a time.

q10.answer: The measure is the canary 5xx ratio over the last minute, read from Prometheus with the query in environments.md. Sampling starts once the canary rollout reports ready and runs every 30 seconds for 15 minutes. A failure is any sample above 1%, or three samples in a row with no data. Either one runs canary-off and fails the run.

q11.answer: I did not decide how approvers are told a run is waiting, and the design does not say what information the approval gate shows. The only stated approver notification is the one-line note in #deploys for superseded runs. The CI approval job records who approved and when, which is all I specified.

q12.answer: No automatic rollback happens after a failed stable rollout. In staging, the tags are left unchanged, because rollback would set the image to previous_tag, which may not be what was running. In production, the tags are not written, the prod-deploy lock is kept, and on-call decides the recovery. I did not specify a manual procedure for returning staging to a known image.
